routes.name: Leland's Ledge
routes.overview: A mega 70-ft jug traverse extending the Lizard Ledge line, with good exposure.
routes.beta: A mega 70 ft jug traverse offering good exposure and, per the first ascentionist, 'world class climbing.' The traverse crosses multiple other established lines, so watch for other parties' ropes/climbers while on it.
routes.turnaround: No summit turnaround applies; this is a short traverse, not a summit route.
routes.descent: Walk off or lower depending on end point reached.
routes.detailed_rack: Protected primarily by a fixed handline; use a lanyard/sling to clip in while traversing rather than a standard quickdraw rack.
watch_out: Traverses across multiple other routes — stay alert for other climbers and ropes crossing your path.
routes.pro_needs: Lanyard for the fixed handline; not a typical bolt-ladder climb.
routes.approach: Located at/extending from Lizard Ledge, cataloged under the East Face area of Keechelus Ridge.
routes.descent_text: As a low-angle traverse rather than a vertical pitch, descent depends on where the traverse is exited; a fixed handline lanyard is recommended for protection while traversing.
routes.bail: Traverse can be exited toward whichever adjoining route offers the nearest anchor.

pitch_detail.notes: 70 ft jug traverse along a fixed handline, crossing several other lines.

areas.name: East Face
areas.blurb: Keechelus Ridge's East Face is a single-pitch sport climbing crag near Snoqualmie Pass in Washington's Central-West Cascades, featuring blocky andesite formations with 17 routes ranging from 5.3 to 5.12+, primarily concentrated between 5.8-5.11. The wall sits at approximately 4,700 feet on a ridge dividing Lake Keechelus and Kachess Lake, offering commanding views of the lakes, Mt. Rainier, and Mt. Stuart. Developed primarily through sport climbing bolting by climbers including Leland Windham, the area provides easily accessible high-elevation crag climbing within the Snoqualmie Pass area.",
